transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Yeah, so, um... work sent me. Basically, I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, and even basic follow-ups I promised people. It's just gotten so bad, and it's piled up so much that my boss was like, "You need to get this sorted before you lose your shot at moving up." Which, honestly, is so frustrating because I've been at this company for, what, six years now? And I know the systems inside and out. Like, just last week, we got this new shipment of HVAC filters, the MERV 13 ones, which are supposed to be better for allergens, and I was telling my sister about it because her kids have terrible allergies. Oh, she lives out in the valley, and the dust out there is just awful this time of year. Anyway, I don't even know how we got on that. But yeah, the work orders. I just... I keep dropping the ball, and they told me I had to come see someone.
Have you noticed problems with forgetfulness, distractibility, or staying on task since you were a child, or is this something that's really only become noticeable recently?

Oh, no, it's definitely not just recently. I remember being exactly like this way back in grade school, long before any of this job pressure started. My teachers always used to tell my parents that I was bright, but I was just constantly misplacing my papers. 

I remember my third-grade classroom had those old wooden desks where the whole top lifts up? The hinges on those things were just terrible, always squeaking or getting totally jammed. Honestly, looking back as a maintenance worker, if I went in there now I could probably fix the whole row of them in ten minutes. I actually keep a little can of silicone lubricant in my tool belt for things exactly like that—well, usually I do. I think I might have left it on top of the water heater in the basement yesterday. Or maybe it rolled under my truck seat. 

Wait, what was I saying? 

Oh, right, school. Yeah, so I'd lose my worksheets in those messy desks, and I'd always miss parts of the directions the teacher gave out out loud. I'd do the first step of a project and then just... drift off. They constantly had to come over and tap on my desk to give me reminders just to finish my classwork. So, yeah, it's not new. It's been like this for as long as I can remember.
Growing up and even now, have you often felt restless, fidgety, or like you had to be constantly moving, or found yourself interrupting others or acting impulsively?

No, not really. I mean, I'm not bouncing off the walls or anything. I don't really interrupt people either. I'm more of a listener, you know? Unless we're talking about plumbing. Then I can talk for hours. 

Speaking of which, I had this one job last month, a real nightmare. The pipes were so old, galvanized steel, probably from the fifties. You know how those corrode from the inside out? It's a disaster waiting to happen. I always tell people, if you're buying an older home, get the plumbing inspected first. My cousin bought a place in Austin, beautiful mid-century modern, but the pipes were shot. Cost her a fortune to repipe the whole house. And she's got these three big dogs, so having the water shut off for days was just miserable for them. One of them is a Great Dane mix, huge thing, eats like a horse. 

But no, to answer your question, I don't really get restless or impulsive like that. Just... easily distracted, I guess.
Aside from work, do these same problems with forgetfulness and losing track of things also cause noticeable difficulties at home or in your personal relationships?

At home? I mean, I guess things get a little messy. My husband gets frustrated when I forget to pay the water bill or leave my boots in the hallway, but... actually, speaking of water, we had this massive leak under our kitchen sink last month. The previous owner used those cheap plastic push-to-connect fittings, and I always say those are just a ticking time bomb. You really need copper or at least PEX with proper brass crimp rings. I ended up having to rip out the whole base of the cabinet to fix it, which was a real shame because it was solid oak, not that particle board garbage they use in all the new builds now. You can't even find good oak at the big box stores anymore, you have to go to a specialty lumber yard. There's a great one out on Route 9, right next to this little diner that makes the absolute best cherry pie. My dad used to take me there when I was a kid. 

Wait, what did you ask me? 

Oh, right, if it causes problems at home. Honestly, the home stuff isn't even what's keeping me up at night. It's work. That's the real nightmare. Like I was saying earlier, the problems have turned into a serious work issue now. I have this massive backlog of tickets, and it's gotten to the point where I'm getting actual tenant complaints because I keep forgetting to go back and finish their repairs. I even got a safety review put on my record recently. I'm just so scared it may cost me the promotion path I’ve been working toward for years. If I lose that... I just don't know what I'll do.
Over the past several months, have you been feeling persistently sad, anxious, or low in energy, in a way that's different from how you've always been?

Sad or anxious? Um... I don't think so. Not persistently, anyway. I mean, I'm stressed about work, obviously, like I said. But I don't feel sad or anything like that. My energy is fine. Actually, I probably have more energy than half the guys on my crew. 

You should see my coworker, Dave. The guy is practically asleep on his feet by 2 PM every day. I keep telling him he needs to stop drinking those huge energy drinks from the gas station—they just give you a crash later. I stick to black coffee. My husband got me this really nice French press for our anniversary last year, and it makes such a difference. You have to use a coarse grind, though, otherwise you get all this sludge at the bottom of your cup. I usually buy my beans from this little local roaster downtown. They have this Ethiopian blend that is just incredible, really bright and fruity. 

But, uh, no, I'm not feeling sad or low energy or anything. Just... stressed about my job.
How has your sleep been lately—are you getting enough restful sleep most nights, and do you use any substances like alcohol, marijuana, or stimulant medications regularly?

Sleep? I sleep like a rock, honestly. As soon as my head hits the pillow, I'm out. My husband, though, he snores like a freight train. He finally got one of those CPAP machines a few months ago. The funny thing is, the cord on that machine was so short, and our bedroom only had one outlet on the far wall. People always just run extension cords under the rug for that kind of stuff, which is a huge fire hazard. I see it all the time at the apartment complex—tenants daisy-chaining cheap power strips for their TVs and space heaters. It drives me absolutely crazy. 

So anyway, I ended up cutting into the drywall and wiring a new 15-amp receptacle right next to his nightstand. I had to fish the wire down from the attic, which was awful because it’s just crawling with old fiberglass insulation up there. I was itching for days. And then patching the wall after? Getting the texture to match that old 1970s plaster is a complete nightmare. You have to use this special sponge technique, and even then, if the afternoon light hits it wrong, you can still see the seam... 

Wait, what was the rest of your question? 

Oh, right, substances and stuff. No, no drugs or marijuana or anything like that. I don't take any pills either. I might have a beer if we're grilling burgers on a weekend, but that's about it. So yeah, sleep is totally fine. No issues there.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a lifelong (since grade school) pattern of significant inattention—losing materials, missing instructions, failing to complete tasks, being easily distracted by tangential thoughts (evident throughout the interview itself)—that now causes clear functional impairment at work (missed work orders, tenant complaints, safety review, risk to promotion) and mild impairment at home. Hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (restlessness, interrupting, impulsivity) are explicitly denied. Mood symptoms (sadness, anxiety, low energy), sleep disturbance, and substance use are all denied, making primary mood, anxiety, or substance-induced attentional disturbance unlikely. The chronicity (childhood onset), cross-situational impairment (school, home, work), and predominant inattentive-type presentation without hyperactivity support a diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation, coded under ICD-10 as F90.0 (Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder).
